title: Tracking experiments: runs, seeds, and knowing what made the difference

videos.script: You change one setting, train again, and the accuracy goes up. Did your change do that? {{question}} Run the same program with another seed, and the number moves anyway. {{seeds}} A seed fixes the starting weights and the order of the batches. Same seed, same network, to the last bit. {{spread}} Five seeds of one configuration landed four images apart, out of three hundred and sixty. Nobody chose those four images. That spread is the yardstick. {{compare}} A wider hidden layer won on one seed and lost on another. Over five seeds, it changed nothing. A higher learning rate beat every seed of the old one. That difference is real. {{record}} To know which run was which, each one writes a line. The settings, the seed, the commit, the data and the library versions. {{dirty}} A run from code nobody committed is marked, and kept out of the report. {{determinism}} Then the limits: why the same seed can still differ on another machine, or on a graphics card. {{tools}} And the tools teams use instead of a file, and what they add. {{end}}
